hypothesis.h0: Evidence bound to a mutated fingerprint component can still satisfy current compatibility.
hypothesis.h1: Every single-component fingerprint mutation causes the compatibility check to fail closed.

falsification: The freshness and compatibility rules are refuted by a single run in which evidence bound to a mutated fingerprint component satisfies current compatibility. The gate is a fail-closed rate of 1.0 with zero observed failures over 20 seeds per enumerated mutation (6 mutations x 20 seeds = 120 runs). The Clopper-Pearson 95% interval is reported so the residual uncertainty at n = 20 stays visible; it does not license a nonzero failure rate.

conditions.description: verified candidate with an intact fingerprint; the control
verified candidate with exactly one fingerprint component mutated

workloads: one verified candidate fixture per enumerated mutation
population.sampling: enumerated fault x seed grid; every mutation receives every seed

effect_size.unit: fail-closed rate; zero observed failures required

analysis_plan.stopping_rule: fixed grid; any observed failure stops the run and files a defect

exclusion_rule: A run is excluded only when the fault injector itself fails to inject the enumerated fault, verified from the injector log. A run in which the fault was injected and the system did not fail closed is a failure, never an exclusion.

environment.source_commit: pinned at run time; the exact commit is recorded in each run.json

threats: a mutation that the canonicalization scheme normalizes away, masking a real gap; each mutation asserts a changed fingerprint digest before the compatibility check runs
